title: Uniform supported lifting from coordinate faces
statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and let $D\subseteq\mathbf N^n$ satisfy $D+\mathbf N^n=D$ and $\alpha-\alpha_p e_p+\alpha_p e_v\in D$ for $\alpha\in D$ and $p<v$, with $e_j$ the $j$th coordinate vector. List its coordinatewise minimal elements $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_s$ in increasing lexicographic order of $(|\alpha|,\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)$. Put $d_i=|\alpha_i|$, $\Delta_i=\{\beta:\alpha_i+\beta\notin\bigcup_{h<i}(\alpha_h+\mathbf N^n)\}$, $\Delta_0=\mathbf N^n\setminus D$, $d=\max(\{0\}\cup\{d_i\})$, $M=\max(1,d)$ and $b=d+n(M-1)+1$. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $H_i\in A[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]$ be homogeneous of degrees $d_i$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Write $V_k$ for the homogeneous degree-$k$ submodule and
$$\mathcal P_k=\{Y^\beta H_i:\beta\in\Delta_i,\ |\beta|+d_i=k\}\amalg\{Y^\gamma:\gamma\in\Delta_0,\ |\gamma|=k\}$$
as an indexed family [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. For $0\le r<n$ let $F_r=\{\beta:\beta_1=\cdots=\beta_r=0\}$ and let $\rho_r$ set $Y_1,\ldots,Y_r$ to zero. If $k\ge b$, then $\beta\in\Delta_i\cap F_r$, $|\beta|+d_i=k$ implies $\beta+e_{r+1}\in\Delta_i$; likewise $\gamma\in\Delta_0\cap F_r$, $|\gamma|=k$ implies $\gamma+e_{r+1}\in\Delta_0$. If additionally $\mathcal P_k$ spans $V_k$, then $\rho_r(\mathcal P_k)$ spans the degree-$k$ polynomials in the remaining variables; generators whose multiplier has a positive coordinate among the first $r$ have zero image. Every homogeneous degree-$(k+1)$ polynomial $P\in A[Y_{r+1},\ldots,Y_n]$ divisible by $Y_{r+1}$ admits $Q\in\operatorname{Span}_A\mathcal P_{k+1}$ with $\rho_r(Q)=P$. The bound $b$ is independent of $A$ and of the $H_i$, and the assertions include empty and full diagrams.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 for the inherited route; Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Definition 8.3, Remarks 8.4 and Lemma 8.5, printed pp.274--275: exceptional-degree bound, restricted spanning and coordinate-face lifts; explicit larger bound from lem-trf-monotone-diagram-face-exceptions. Journal PDF read online at https://mahalex.net/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf. No Stacks tag states this specialized result; BM paper absent from repository literature.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-monotone-diagram-face-exceptions] to this same $D$, vertex order and face $F_r$; its $M$ equals $\max(1,d)$. If $\beta\in\Delta_i\cap F_r$ but $\beta+e_{r+1}\notin\Delta_i$, its box bound gives $|\beta|\le(n-r)(M-1)\le n(M-1)$. Thus $|\beta|+d_i\le n(M-1)+d=b-1$, contradicting $|\beta|+d_i=k\ge b$. For a remainder exponent $\gamma\in\Delta_0\cap F_r$, the same exceptional-box conclusion gives $|\gamma|\le n(M-1)\le b-1$, again contradicting $|\gamma|=k\ge b$. This proves both support-stability assertions.

proof.text: By coefficientwise polynomial evaluation [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $\rho_r(Y^\eta)$ is zero if some $\eta_j>0$ with $j\le r$, and otherwise is the same monomial in the remaining variables. Consequently $\rho_r(Y^\beta H_i)=\rho_r(Y^\beta)\rho_r(H_i)$, so every generator with a multiplier outside $F_r$ vanishes. Evaluation preserves each homogeneous degree: it deletes monomials and leaves the exponents and coefficients of the surviving ones unchanged. Inclusion of the remaining-variable polynomial ring is a section of $\rho_r$.

proof.text: Assume now that $\mathcal P_k$ spans $V_k$ in the sense of [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. Given a degree-$k$ polynomial $T$ in the remaining variables, include it in $V_k$ and express it as a finite $A$-linear combination of the indexed generators. Applying $\rho_r$ to that equality preserves its coefficients and sums, by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and fixes $T$. Step 2 deletes all terms with multipliers outside $F_r$. The surviving images therefore span all degree-$k$ polynomials in the remaining variables.

proof.text: Let $P$ have degree $k+1$ in the remaining variables and be divisible by $Y_{r+1}$. In the monomial description [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], divisibility forces every nonzero monomial of $P$ to have positive $(r+1)$st exponent: multiplication by that variable shifts every exponent by $e_{r+1}$. Subtract $e_{r+1}$ from each exponent of $P$ to obtain a finite homogeneous degree-$k$ polynomial $T$ with $Y_{r+1}T=P$. Use Step 3 to write $T=\sum_{\lambda}c_\lambda\rho_r(G_\lambda)$ with surviving indexed generators $G_\lambda\in\mathcal P_k$. By Step 1, $Y_{r+1}G_\lambda$ is an indexed generator of $\mathcal P_{k+1}$: its multiplier becomes $\beta+e_{r+1}$, or its remainder exponent becomes $\gamma+e_{r+1}$, and its degree increases by one [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. Set $Q=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda Y_{r+1}G_\lambda$. Then $Q\in\operatorname{Span}_A\mathcal P_{k+1}$ and $\rho_r(Q)=Y_{r+1}\sum_\lambda c_\lambda\rho_r(G_\lambda)=P$.

proof.text: The number $b=d+n(M-1)+1$ uses only the diagram and $n$, hence neither $A$ nor $H_i$. If $D=\varnothing$, there are no vertex terms, $d=0$, $M=1$, $b=1$, and all monomials are remainder generators. If $D=\mathbf N^n$, the single vertex is $0$, $\Delta_1=\mathbf N^n$ and $\Delta_0=\varnothing$; the same argument uses only the assumed spanning and remains valid. For $r=0$ evaluation is the identity, and for $r=n-1$ only one variable remains; both are already covered. The coefficient formulas also hold in the zero ring and with vanishing $H_i$.

Step 5: b depends only on the diagram, and D=∅ and D=ℕⁿ (both b=1), r=0, r=n−1, the zero ring and H_i=0 are all correct.
